# Research notes: governorate crop statistics for the Nile Delta model

Access date for every source in this file: 14 November 2026.

Purpose. These notes document every series saved in this folder, so that any number in the model can be traced to a named, dated, public source. Where a number could not be obtained, the notes say so in plain words. No number in the CSV files was invented, estimated by me, or carried over from the old illustrative model inputs.

A note on sources. The task asked for CAPMAS, the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (الجهاز المركزي للتعبئة العامة والإحصاء), and its annual bulletin of crop areas and plant production statistics (نشرة إحصاءات المساحات المحصولية والإنتاج النباتي). The full CAPMAS bulletin PDFs for the recent years 2019 to 2024 could not be obtained as open files during this research, despite searches in Arabic and English across capmas.gov.eg, the CAPMAS metadata catalogue, and general web search. What could be obtained in full, openly, and at governorate level is the underlying official series itself: the Agricultural Statistics Bulletins of the Economic Affairs Sector (قطاع الشئون الاقتصادية) of the Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation (وزارة الزراعة واستصلاح الأراضي), published at agri.gov.eg. CAPMAS states in its own bulletin methodology that its crop area and plant production data are collected from the Ministry of Agriculture, and the Ministry tables are the same governorate tables, with the same structure of old land, new land, and total, that CAPMAS republishes. The Ministry series is therefore treated here as first hand evidence for the same statistics. Every CAPMAS item that was located but not extracted is listed as such in the located but unextracted section, and the gap section states plainly what is still missing.

Units and conversions used in all CSV files in this folder. Published area unit: feddan (فدان). Published production unit: ton (طن). Published yield unit in the main Ministry tables: tons per feddan. The one conversion applied is the project rule: 1 feddan equals 0.42 hectares exactly. Converted area in hectares equals published feddan multiplied by 0.42. Converted yield in tons per hectare equals published tons per feddan divided by 0.42. Production needs no conversion because it is already published in tons. The Ministry bulletins also republish wheat and maize in ardab tables. For the record, the bulletins give 1 ardab of wheat as 0.150 ton and 1 ardab of maize as 0.140 ton in their units tables. The ardab tables were used only as a cross check; all saved values come from the tons tables.

## Series 1. Ministry of Agriculture, Agricultural Statistics Bulletin Part 1, Winter Crops, agricultural year 2020/2021

Source name in English: Agricultural Statistics Bulletin, Part 1, Winter Crops, 2021. Source name in Arabic: نشرة الإحصاءات الزراعية، الجزء الأول، المحاصيل الشتوية. Publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, Economic Affairs Sector, Egypt. URL: https://www.agri.gov.eg/uploads/topics/16595251012198.pdf Years covered: agricultural year 2020/2021, winter season. Crops saved: wheat from Table 2, sugar beet from Table 12. Governorates saved: all 8 Delta governorates. Published units: area in feddan, yield in tons per feddan, production in tons. Values saved are the total columns of each table, meaning old land plus new land combined. National totals printed in the same tables, for cross checking only: wheat 3419427 feddan and 9842272 tons; sugar beet 682771 feddan and 14195489 tons.

## Series 2. Ministry of Agriculture, Agricultural Statistics Bulletin Part 2, Summer and Nili Crops, agricultural year 2020/2021

Source name in English: Agricultural Statistics Bulletin, Part 2, Summer and Nili Crops. Source name in Arabic: نشرة الإحصاءات الزراعية، الجزء الثاني، المحاصيل الصيفية والنيلية. Publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, Economic Affairs Sector, Egypt. URL: https://www.agri.gov.eg/uploads/topics/16692385498467.pdf Years covered: agricultural year 2020/2021, summer and Nili seasons. Crops saved: rice from Table 20 (summer), maize from Table 22 (summer, white and yellow maize combined), potatoes for all seasons combined from Table 78, winter potatoes from Table 79, summer potatoes from Table 80, Nili potatoes from Table 81. Governorates saved: all 8 Delta governorates. Published units: area in feddan, yield in tons per feddan, production in tons. Two facts about coverage inside this bulletin. First, Table 20 lists no row for Menoufia rice at all; the CSV files record this as not reported in source table, and the value was not set to zero. Second, Table 81 lists Nili potatoes only for Beheira, Gharbia, and Menoufia among the Delta governorates; the other five are recorded as not reported in source table. This bulletin also supplied the land base series: total cropped area by governorate from Table 19 and cultivated area by governorate from Table 17, both for agricultural year 2020/2021. National totals printed in the bulletin: total cropped area 16375026 feddan, cultivated area 9596480 feddan, rice 1104862 feddan and 4241894 tons, summer maize 2246903 feddan and 7447935 tons, potatoes all seasons 502552 feddan and 6273931 tons. Nili maize by governorate sits in Tables 27 to 31 of this same bulletin and was located but not extracted; see the located but unextracted section.

## Series 5. Land base series, total cropped area and cultivated area by governorate

Saved in capmas_governorate_total_cropped_area.csv. Sources: Series 2 above (Tables 17 and 19, agricultural year 2020/2021) and Series 4 above (Table 19, agricultural year 2019/2020). The measure column in the CSV keeps three different concepts apart, and they must not be mixed. Total cropped area counts every crop season in the year, so one physical feddan planted twice counts twice. Cultivated area counts the physical land inside the agricultural boundary once. Zemam area is the registered agricultural land area from the separate CAPMAS bulletin on land tenure (نشرة الزمام والملكية الزراعية). For a district land base in the model, cultivated area is the physical land concept and total cropped area is the planting intensity concept; the choice between them is a modelling decision, and both are provided.

## Series 6. Second hand. Menoufia wheat and maize from a 2025 study quoting CAPMAS bulletins

Source name in English: Analysis of wheat and maize productivity in Menoufia under climate change pressures, City Researchers Programme, second edition 2024, published 2025. Source name in Arabic: تحليل لإنتاجية القمح والذرة في المنوفية تحت ضغوط التغير المناخي. Publisher: Human and City Studies (الإنسان والمدينة), hcsr-eg.org. URL: https://www.hcsr-eg.org/media/2025/05/تحليل-لإنتاجية-القمح-والذرة-في-المنوفية-تحت-ضغوط-التغير-المناخي_باحثي-المدينة.pdf The study quotes the CAPMAS bulletin of crop areas and plant production for 2021/2022 and 2022/2023. Values saved, Menoufia only: wheat area and production for 2021/2022 and 2022/2023; white maize area and production for both years; yellow maize area and production for both years; a combined maize row that I computed by adding the white and yellow rows, labelled as computed in the CSV files. The study publishes area and production but not yield for these rows, so the yields in capmas_governorate_yield.csv for this source are computed from the published area and production and are flagged as computed, never as published. The same study gives Menoufia total cropped area for 2022/2023 as 608610 feddan, Menoufia cultivated area for 2022/2023 as 300111 feddan, and Menoufia zemam area from the CAPMAS zemam bulletin of 2023 as 448413 feddan. All of this series is labelled second hand in the CSV files because it was read in the study, not in the CAPMAS bulletin itself.

## Series 7. Second hand, use with caution. Cropped area and rice area table in a conference paper citing CAPMAS 2024

Source name in English: Statistical Spatial Modeling of Agricultural Waste Using Geographic Information Systems, A Case Study of the Nile Delta, by Wafaa Ezzat Ali Eid of CAPMAS, submitted to the tenth International Conference on Agricultural Statistics, ICAS X 2026, submission 3930. URL: https://www.isi-next.org/media/abstracts/icas-x-2026_d9c87f70af275050936ed266b9b24a51.pdf Table 2 of the paper is labelled Source: CAPMAS, 2024 and gives, for each Delta governorate, a total cropped area and a rice cropped area in feddan. The paper does not state which agricultural year these cropped area columns describe. The values are saved in a separate file, capmas_secondhand_isi_cropped_and_rice_area.csv, and not merged into the main series, for two stated reasons. The printed national total cropped area in the paper, 12418324 feddan, does not reconcile with the CAPMAS national cropped area of 16800000 feddan for 2022/2023 or 16375026 feddan for 2020/2021. The Menoufia cropped area in the paper, 455869 feddan, also conflicts with the 608610 feddan given for 2022/2023 by Series 6. Until the definition behind the paper table is verified, this series is evidence of what a CAPMAS author published, not a land base the model should use.

## Series 8. National context only, CAPMAS press release for the bulletin of 2022/2023

Source name in English: CAPMAS press release announcing the annual bulletin of crop areas and plant production statistics for 2022/2023, issued 23 December 2024. Source name in Arabic: النشرة السنوية لإحصاءات المساحات المحصولية والإنتاج النباتي عام 2022/2023. Publisher: CAPMAS, release copy hosted by the State Information Service. URL: https://mediadr.sis.gov.eg:443/bitstream/handle/123456789/85135/CAPMAS20241223_020.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y Figures in the release are national only and were not saved into the governorate CSV files: total cropped area 16.8 million feddan in 2022/2023 against 16.6 million in 2021/2022; cultivated area 9.8 million feddan against 9.7 million; wheat 3.2 million feddan and 9.1 million tons in 2022/2023 against 3.4 million feddan and 9.6 million tons in 2021/2022; rice 1.6 million feddan and 6.2 million tons in 2022/2023 against 1.1 million feddan and 4.3 million tons; potatoes 649.0 thousand feddan and 8.6 million tons in 2022/2023 against 584.8 thousand feddan and 7.2 million tons. This release proves the CAPMAS bulletin for 2022/2023 exists and was published. Its governorate tables were not obtained.

## Located but unextracted

CAPMAS bulletin of crop areas and plant production statistics for 2010/2011 (إحصاءات المساحات المحصولية والإنتاج النباتى عام 2010/2011), issued November 2011, CAPMAS reference 20 00402 of 2011, full text at https://metadata.capmas.gov.eg/ar/index.php/catalog/598/download/2725 The front matter, contents, and methodology were read. The contents confirm the structure the model needs: Chapter 1 gives total cropped area and cultivated area by governorate, and later chapters give winter, summer, and Nili crops by governorate. The governorate data tables of this edition were not extracted in this pass. Status: located but unextracted. It would provide a CAPMAS direct historical anchor year, 2010/2011, outside the 2019 to 2024 window.

Nili maize by governorate for agricultural year 2020/2021 sits in Tables 27 to 31 of the Series 2 bulletin at https://www.agri.gov.eg/uploads/topics/16692385498467.pdf The tables were located in the bulletin contents but their governorate rows were not extracted in this pass. Status: located but unextracted. Effect: the saved maize series is summer maize only. National Nili maize area for 2021 is printed in the same bulletin as 124428 feddan of white maize plus 71944 feddan of yellow maize, so Nili maize is a real addition of roughly 9 percent on top of the national summer maize area, and it matters most for Menoufia and Qalyubia.

The Ministry library pages at agri.gov.eg list further bulletin editions, including Part 1 and Part 2 volumes for 2022, 2023, and 2025, at https://www.agri.gov.eg/library/71 and https://www.agri.gov.eg/library/25 Several entries state that a login is required to view the file. The direct file links used for Series 1 to 4 bypass that wall; no direct file link for a Part 2 summer bulletin of 2023/2024 or later was found. Status: located but unextracted, behind a login wall.

## Gap list, stated plainly

No CAPMAS direct governorate table for any year from 2019 to 2024 was obtained as a CAPMAS file. The governorate panel in the CSV files is first hand from the Ministry bulletins that supply CAPMAS, not from CAPMAS publications themselves.

No governorate data at all was obtained for agricultural year 2021/2022, except the second hand Menoufia wheat and maize figures in Series 6.

No governorate data was obtained for agricultural year 2022/2023, except the second hand Menoufia figures in Series 6 and the national totals in Series 8.

For agricultural year 2023/2024, only the winter season is covered (wheat, sugar beet, winter potatoes). Rice, maize, summer potatoes, and total cropped area by governorate for 2023/2024 were not obtained.

For agricultural year 2019/2020, only the summer season is covered (rice, maize, potatoes all seasons, total cropped area). Wheat, sugar beet, and the seasonal potato split for 2019/2020 were not obtained.

Nothing was obtained for agricultural year 2024/2025 at governorate level. A CAPMAS national statement reports wheat production of 10.0 million tons and rice production of 5.1 million tons for 2024/2025, but no governorate split was published in any source reached.

Menoufia rice for agricultural year 2020/2021 is not reported in the source table. It is recorded as missing, not as zero. Menoufia rice for 2019/2020 is reported as 19 feddan, which shows how small rice planting in Menoufia is, but the 2020/2021 cell itself remains unverified.

Nili maize by governorate was not extracted for any year, so all saved maize figures are summer season only and understate full year maize area.

No source reached breaks any governorate down further, to markaz or district level, for these crops and years. Governorate is the finest geography obtained.

## Files saved in this folder from this research

capmas_governorate_area.csv holds cropped area by governorate, crop, season, and agricultural year, in feddan as published and in hectares converted. capmas_governorate_production.csv holds production in tons as published. capmas_governorate_yield.csv holds yield in tons per feddan as published, or computed where the flag says so, and in tons per hectare converted. capmas_governorate_total_cropped_area.csv holds the land base measures. capmas_secondhand_isi_cropped_and_rice_area.csv holds the Series 7 table on its own, with its warning attached. Every row carries a source identifier matching the series numbers in these notes, the table number inside the source where one exists, an evidence grade of first hand or second hand, and a data status.
